findings.title: Foreign XML namespaces can masquerade as NuGet or Maven declarations and create false framework facts

evidence.detail: NuGet owner validation recognizes Project, Sdk, PackageReference, and FrameworkReference solely through Name.LocalName.
Direct NuGet parsing similarly ignores element namespaces.
Maven project, dependencies, dependency, groupId, and artifactId selection uses LocalName without namespace validation.
The malformed and duplicate XML suite has no namespace-spoofing case.

documented_standard: docs/bmad/implementation-artifacts/4-2-language-and-framework-detection.md:73-82 requires closed deterministic package declarations and no invented facts.
specs/002-language-framework-detection/contracts/framework-detection.md:46-55 permits only literal NuGet/Maven evidence and requires unsupported evidence to create no fact.
.specify/memory/constitution.md:67-89 requires deterministic domain facts and authoritative ubiquitous language.
findings.impact: A committed pom.xml or .csproj can place catalog-matching local names in a foreign namespace. The detector treats those non-Maven or non-MSBuild elements as genuine declarations and persists a High-confidence framework fact.
findings.correction_outcome: Validate supported root namespaces and require every consumed XML element to belong to the root's supported namespace. Foreign-namespace lookalikes create no fact, remain artifact-local with one bounded closed audit, and do not suppress independent valid evidence. Add RED/GREEN coverage for NuGet direct evidence, NuGet lock ownership, Maven evidence, mixed legitimate and foreign elements, and standard namespace or no-namespace documents.

findings.title: Committed-tree inventory is unbounded before the supported-artifact limit is applied

evidence.detail: ls-tree enumerates the entire pinned tree; ReadToEndAsync, Split, List, and the returned array materialize every tracked entry without a byte or record bound.
The complete inventory is duplicated into arrays, a dictionary, and sets before RecordSupportedArtifact applies the 1,000-artifact limit.
Coverage proves overflow for supported artifacts, but not an arbitrarily large inventory of unrelated tracked paths or bounded inventory output.

documented_standard: specs/002-language-framework-detection/contracts/framework-detection.md:110-129 defines repository bounds and fail-closed behavior.
findings.impact: A Repository with very many irrelevant tracked files bypasses detector counters and can force large stdout strings plus several full inventory copies, exhausting process memory before a typed fail-closed result is available.
findings.correction_outcome: Enumerate only the six supported committed artifact shapes through pinned-tree pathspecs, or parse ls-tree incrementally with explicit byte, record, and deadline bounds before materialization. Preserve commit, tree, and object-mode integrity. Add RED/GREEN cases for huge irrelevant inventories, bounded-output overflow, cancellation, and zero partial facts. Reconcile stale contract, plan, and story wording that still claims git ls-files --cached.

quality_assessment.test_quality: REVISE due to the two missing adversarial cases; existing provider, transaction, API, UI, migration, QR7 duplicate, and committed-source tests are otherwise substantial.
quality_assessment.architecture_seams: Layering, EF configuration, additive migrations, atomic profile persistence and recovery, API authorization and redaction, DTO boundaries, and Chinese UI localization are sound in the reviewed boundary.
quality_assessment.regression_risk: High until both findings are corrected through authorized RED-GREEN work and both Full review axes are rerun.
quality_assessment.forbidden_scope: No Worker Agent/tool, orchestration, dispatch, scheduling, retry, PRD weakening, or document-generation implementation was found.

summary: REVISE. Two High findings block advancement: XML namespace spoofing can persist fabricated framework facts, and committed-tree inventory can exhaust memory before repository bounds apply.
